entries.goal: What is the current UTC time?
Get the current time in Tokyo, London, and New York. Tell me which one is the furthest ahead of UTC.
It is 09:00 in Tokyo. What time is that in New York and in London? Use the convert_time tool to get exact answers.
Fetch https://example.com and tell me the single sentence that describes what the domain is reserved for.
Fetch https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains and quote one sentence that mentions which RFC reserves the example.com domain.
Check the status and last 3 commits of the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo. Tell me whether the working tree is clean and what the most recent commit message was.
In the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo create a branch named 'feature/scaled-run' and confirm it appears in the branch list.

In the sqlite database, create a table called 'people' with columns id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and name TEXT NOT NULL. Insert one row (id=1, name='Ada'). Then read back all rows and tell me the name you stored.
List all tables currently in the sqlite database. If there are any, describe the schema of the first one. If there are none, say so explicitly.
In the filesystem sandbox at /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox, write a file called 'hello.txt' containing the text 'hello from dmcp'. Then read the file back and confirm the contents match.
List all files and directories under /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox and tell me how many entries you found at the top level.

In the knowledge graph, create an entity named 'Ada Lovelace' of type 'person' with the observation 'wrote the first algorithm intended for a machine'. Then read the full graph and confirm the entity is there.

In the knowledge graph, create two entities ('Alan Turing' of type 'person', 'Bombe' of type 'machine') and a relation 'designed' from Turing to the Bombe. Then read the graph back and report the relation you see.

Fetch the page at https://example.com, then get the current UTC time, and report both in one summary that includes the current timestamp and the single sentence describing what example.com is reserved for.

Get the current UTC time, then in the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo create a new branch whose name follows the pattern 'snapshot-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS' using the timestamp you just retrieved. Confirm the branch was created by listing local branches.

In the sqlite database, create a table 'events' with columns id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT and observed_at TEXT. Then get the current UTC time and insert one row whose observed_at value is exactly the timestamp string the time tool returned. Read back the rows and confirm.

Get the current UTC time, then in /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox write a file whose name follows the pattern 'snapshot-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.txt' (using the timestamp you retrieved) and whose contents are the full timestamp string. List the directory to confirm the file exists.

Create a sqlite table 'pages' with columns id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, url TEXT, summary TEXT. Then fetch https://example.com and insert one row where url is 'https://example.com' and summary is the single descriptive sentence you find on the page. Read the rows back to confirm.
Fetch https://example.com and save its content to /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox/example.md. Then list the directory and confirm the file is there.
Fetch https://example.com and create one knowledge-graph entity named 'example.com' of type 'website' with one observation summarizing what the page says about the domain.

In /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox write a new file called 'note.txt' containing 'tracked by git'. Then in the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo create a branch called 'add-note' to keep this work isolated. Confirm the branch exists.

In sqlite, create a table 'snapshots' with columns id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT and label TEXT, insert one row with label='first', and read it back. Then in /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox write a file called 'snapshots.txt' whose contents are exactly the label you stored.

Create two knowledge-graph entities 'Project X' (project) and 'Owner Y' (person), plus a relation 'owns' from Y to X. Then read the graph and write its JSON representation to /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox/graph.json.

Fetch https://example.com. Create a sqlite table 'fetched_pages' (id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, url TEXT, body_excerpt TEXT). Insert one row where url='https://example.com' and body_excerpt is the first sentence of the page. Read the row back, and also write a small text file to /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox/fetched_pages_summary.txt that says how many rows you stored.

Get the current UTC time. Write a file called 'snapshot.txt' into /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox whose contents are the timestamp string. Then in the git repository at /tmp/dmcp-sandbox-repo create a branch whose name encodes the same timestamp ('snapshot-' + compact-timestamp) and confirm it appears in the branch list.

Read all rows from a sqlite table called 'definitely_does_not_exist_yet'. If that fails, create the table with columns id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY and value TEXT, insert one row (id=1, value='recovered'), and read it back.
Try to write a file to /tmp/not-allowed/forbidden.txt. If that path is rejected, fall back to writing the file to /private/tmp/dmcp-fs-sandbox/recovery.txt with contents 'recovered'.
